\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية} (nashra jawwiyya)}{نشرة جوية (nashra jawwiyya)}]{\ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية} (nashra jawwiyya) — a weather forecast}

\label{lesson:AR-C480-nashra-jawwiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to exchange, then the Arabic for to pack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية}}
\textbf{\ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية}} — \emph{nashra jawwiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a weather forecast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شاهدنا} \ar{النشرة} \ar{الجوية} \ar{في} \ar{التلفاز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shāhadnā an-nashra al-jawwiyya fī at-tilfāz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We watched the weather forecast on television.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية}} (\emph{nashra jawwiyya}) is built from two native Arabic words: \emph{nashra}, \textquotedblleft{}a bulletin\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{n-sh-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to spread out\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and \emph{jawwiyya}, \textquotedblleft{}of the air\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{j-w-w} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashra jawwiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashra jawwiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāhadnā an-nashra al-jawwiyya fī at-tilfāz.} — We watched the weather forecast on television.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to exchange, then the Arabic for to pack, then say \emph{nashra jawwiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نشرة} \ar{جوية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A weather forecast\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{درجة} (daraja)}{درجة (daraja)}]{\ar{درجة} (daraja) — a degree; a class (of travel)}

\label{lesson:AR-C480-daraja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to pack, then the Arabic for a weather forecast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{درجة}}
\textbf{\ar{درجة}} — \emph{daraja} — \textquotedblleft{}a degree; a class (of travel)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{درجة} \ar{الحرارة} \ar{مرتفعة} \ar{اليوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat darajat al-ḥarāra murtafiʿa al-yawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The temperature was high today.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{درجات}, \emph{darajāt}.

\emph{darajat al-ḥarāra} is the temperature; \emph{ad-daraja al-ūlā} is first class.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{درجة}} (\emph{daraja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to go step by step\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{daraja} is a step.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{daraja}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{daraja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat darajat al-ḥarāra murtafiʿa al-yawm.} — The temperature was high today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to pack, then the Arabic for a weather forecast, then say \emph{daraja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{درجة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A degree; a class (of travel)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ارتفع} (irtafaʿa)}{ارتفع (irtafaʿa)}]{\ar{ارتفع} (irtafaʿa) — to increase; to rise}

\label{lesson:AR-C480-irtafaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a weather forecast, then the Arabic for a degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ارتفع}}
\textbf{\ar{ارتفع}} — \emph{irtafaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to increase; to rise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ارتفعت} \ar{درجة} \ar{الحرارة} \ar{عند} \ar{الظهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{irtafaʿat darajat al-ḥarāra ʿinda aẓ-ẓuhr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The temperature rose at noon.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرتفع}, \emph{yartafiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ارتفع}} (\emph{irtafaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-f-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to raise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to rise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtafaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtafaʿat darajat al-ḥarāra ʿinda aẓ-ẓuhr.} — The temperature rose at noon.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a weather forecast, then the Arabic for a degree, then say \emph{irtafaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انخفض} (inkhafaḍa)}{انخفض (inkhafaḍa)}]{\ar{انخفض} (inkhafaḍa) — to drop; to fall (of a level)}

\label{lesson:AR-C480-inkhafada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a degree, then the Arabic for to increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انخفض}}
\textbf{\ar{انخفض}} — \emph{inkhafaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to drop; to fall (of a level)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انخفضت} \ar{الحرارة} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inkhafaḍat al-ḥarāra fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The temperature dropped at night.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينخفض}, \emph{yankhafiḍ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انخفض}} (\emph{inkhafaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-f-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be low; to lower\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{معتدل} (muʿtadil)}{معتدل (muʿtadil)}]{\ar{معتدل} (muʿtadil) — mild; moderate}

\label{lesson:AR-C480-mutadil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to increase, then the Arabic for to drop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{معتدل}}
\textbf{\ar{معتدل}} — \emph{muʿtadil} — \textquotedblleft{}mild; moderate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الطقس} \ar{في} \ar{الربيع} \ar{معتدل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭ-ṭaqs fī ar-rabīʿ muʿtadil.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather in spring is mild.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{معتدل}} (\emph{muʿtadil}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be even, balanced\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the Form VIII participle, \textquotedblleft{}evenly balanced\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
